pumac-2017-power-01.prompt: **Problem 1.1.1.** Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$ with $\dim V=n<\infty$, where $\dim V$ is the smallest size of a spanning set (a basis is a spanning set of size $\dim V$). Show that any linearly independent set of $n$ vectors in $V$ is a basis of $V$.
pumac-2017-power-01.answer: Independent $n$ vectors that did not span could be extended to $n+1$ independent vectors, impossible in a space spanned by $n$ vectors.

pumac-2017-power-02.prompt: **Problem 1.1.2.** Show that $\mathbb R[x]$ is a real vector space and that $\mathbb C[x]$ is a complex vector space, where $F[x]$ is the set of polynomials of finite degree with coefficients in $F$ (with the usual addition and scalar multiplication). Is $\mathbb R[x]$ a complex vector space? Is $\mathbb C[x]$ a real vector space?
pumac-2017-power-02.answer: $\mathbb R[x]$ is real and $\mathbb C[x]$ is complex; $\mathbb R[x]$ is not a complex vector space (not closed under multiplication by $i$); $\mathbb C[x]$ is a real vector space.

pumac-2017-power-03a.prompt: **Problem 1.2.1(i).** Fix $N\in\mathbb N$ and let $F_N$ be the space of polynomials $a(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}a_nx^n$ over $F$ (degree at most $N$). Determine with proof whether the map $a(x)\mapsto a(x)+a(1)$ from $F_N$ to $F[x]$ is linear.

pumac-2017-power-03b.prompt: **Problem 1.2.1(ii).** Fix $N\in\mathbb N$ and let $F_N$ be the space of polynomials $a(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}a_nx^n$ over $F$ (degree at most $N$). Determine with proof whether the map $a(x)\mapsto a(x)+a(1)x^{N+1}$ from $F_N$ to $F[x]$ is linear.

pumac-2017-power-03c.prompt: **Problem 1.2.1(iii).** Fix $N\in\mathbb N$ and let $F_N$ be the space of polynomials $a(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}a_nx^n$ over $F$ (degree at most $N$). Determine with proof whether the map $a(x)\mapsto \sum_{n=0}^{N}(a_n-a_{N-n})x^n$ from $F_N$ to $F[x]$ is linear.

pumac-2017-power-04.prompt: **Problem 1.2.2.** Describe as precisely as possible all inner products on $\mathbb C^2$. (An inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:V^2\to\mathbb C$ satisfies $\langle x,y\rangle=\overline{\langle y,x\rangle}$, $\langle cx,y\rangle=c\langle x,y\rangle$, $\langle x,z\rangle+\langle y,z\rangle=\langle x+y,z\rangle$, and $\langle x,x\rangle>0$ for $x\ne0$.)
pumac-2017-power-04.answer: $\langle u,v\rangle=r_1u_1\bar v_1+c\,u_1\bar v_2+\bar c\,u_2\bar v_1+r_2u_2\bar v_2$ with $r_1,r_2>0$, $c\in\mathbb C$ and $r_1r_2>|c|^2$ (i.e. $u^T H\bar v$ with $H$ Hermitian positive definite).
pumac-2017-power-04.reviewNote: The official solution gives r1,r2>0 and c nonzero but omits the necessary and sufficient condition r1*r2>|c|^2 (and c=0 is allowed); the stored answer includes it.

pumac-2017-power-05.prompt: **Problem 1.2.3.** Show that if $\varphi:V\to W$ is an isomorphism of vector spaces (a bijective linear map), then $\varphi^{-1}$ is also an isomorphism.

pumac-2017-power-06.prompt: **Problem 1.3.1.** Is matrix multiplication associative? Is it commutative? Explain why or why not.

pumac-2017-power-07.prompt: **Problem 1.3.2.** Let $T_1,T_2:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$ be linear maps with $n\times m$ matrices $\{a_{i,j}\}$ and $\{b_{i,j}\}$ (with respect to fixed bases). Show that $T_1+T_2$ has matrix $\{a_{i,j}+b_{i,j}\}$.
pumac-2017-power-07.answer: The $j$th column of the matrix of $T_1+T_2$ is the sum of the $j$th columns.

pumac-2017-power-08.prompt: **Problem 1.3.3.** Let $T_2:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$ and $T_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p$ be linear maps given by matrices (with the product defined as in the text: $(AB)_{i,j}$ is the dot product of the $i$th row of $A$ with the $j$th column of $B$). Show that $T_1(T_2v)=(T_1T_2)v$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^m$, i.e. the matrix of the composite is the product of the matrices.
pumac-2017-power-08.answer: Composition of maps corresponds to the matrix product.

pumac-2017-power-09.prompt: **Problem 2.1.1.** Let $M$ be a linear map of $V$ and $V_\lambda=\{v\in V: Mv=\lambda v\}$. Show that $V_\lambda$ is a subspace of $V$.
pumac-2017-power-09.answer: $V_\lambda$ is closed under linear combinations and contains $0$.

pumac-2017-power-10.prompt: **Problem 2.1.2.** Why does any linear map $M$ of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ have only finitely many distinct eigenvalues?
pumac-2017-power-10.answer: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent, so there are at most $\dim V$ eigenvalues.

pumac-2017-power-11.prompt: **Problem 2.1.3.** Let $M:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be the linear map with matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&7\end{pmatrix}$. Find every eigenvector and the corresponding eigenvalue of $M$.

pumac-2017-power-12.prompt: **Problem 2.1.4.** For each of the linear maps from Problem 1.2.1, determine its eigenvalues and classify as well as you can the corresponding eigenvectors. The maps are defined on polynomials $a(x)=\sum_{n=0}^Na_nx^n$ of degree at most $N$: $f_1(a)=a(x)+a(1)$; $f_2(a)=a(x)+a(1)x^{N+1}$; $f_3(a)=\sum_{n=0}^N(a_n-a_{N-n})x^n$.
pumac-2017-power-12.answer: $f_1$: eigenvalue $1$ (polynomials with $a(1)=0$) and $2$ (nonzero constants). $f_2$: only eigenvalue $1$ (polynomials with $a(1)=0$). $f_3$: eigenvalue $0$ (palindromic: $a_n=a_{N-n}$) and $2$ (antipalindromic: $a_n=-a_{N-n}$).

pumac-2017-power-13.prompt: **Problem 2.2.1.** Let $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ be the set of $n\times n$ complex matrices of trace $0$. What is $\dim\mathfrak{sl}_n$? Find a basis.
pumac-2017-power-13.answer: $n^2-1$; basis $e_{i,j}$ ($i\neq j$) together with $e_{i,i}-e_{i+1,i+1}$ ($1\le i\le n-1$).

pumac-2017-power-14.prompt: **Problem 2.2.2.** Let $R_{2n}=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$, $R_{2n+1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&R_{2n}\end{pmatrix}$, $\tilde R_{2n}=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_n\\-I_n&0\end{pmatrix}$. Let $\mathfrak{so}_m=\{M\in\mathfrak{gl}_m: M^TR_m+R_mM=0\}$ and $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}=\{M\in\mathfrak{gl}_{2n}:M^T\tilde R_{2n}+\tilde R_{2n}M=0\}$. Describe the elements of $\mathfrak{so}_m$ and $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}$ as precisely as you can and find $\dim\mathfrak{so}_{2n}$, $\dim\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}$, $\dim\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}$.

pumac-2017-power-15.prompt: **Problem 2.3.1.** Show that if $X$ and $Y$ are $n\times n$ complex matrices that commute and $X$ is nilpotent, then $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=0$.
pumac-2017-power-15.answer: $XY$ is nilpotent, hence has all eigenvalues $0$ and trace $0$.

pumac-2017-power-16.prompt: **Problem 3.1.1.** Let $[f,g]=f\circ g-g\circ f$ for $f,g\in\mathfrak{gl}_n$. Show that the Jacobi identity holds, and therefore that $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ is a Lie algebra.
pumac-2017-power-16.answer: Expand the three double brackets; the terms cancel in pairs.

pumac-2017-power-17.prompt: **Problem 3.1.2.** Explain why two Lie algebras of different dimension cannot be isomorphic.
pumac-2017-power-17.answer: An isomorphism is in particular a linear bijection, which preserves dimension.

pumac-2017-power-18.prompt: **Problem 3.1.3.** Show that two (finite-dimensional) abelian Lie algebras $L_1,L_2$ are isomorphic if and only if they have the same dimension.
pumac-2017-power-18.answer: Any linear isomorphism between abelian Lie algebras preserves the (zero) bracket.

pumac-2017-power-19.prompt: **Problem 3.1.4.** In a Lie algebra $L$, assume $[x,[y,z]]=[[x,y],z]$ for all $x,y,z\in L$. What is the most general statement you can make about elements of $L$?
pumac-2017-power-19.answer: The assumption holds iff $[x,[y,z]]=0$ for all $x,y,z$, i.e. $[L,L]\subseteq Z(L)$ (the center).

pumac-2017-power-20a.prompt: **Problem 3.1.5(i).** Let $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ have basis $v_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ with bracket $[A,B]=AB-BA$, so $[v_3,v_1]=2v_1$, $[v_3,v_2]=-2v_2$, $[v_1,v_2]=v_3$. Suppose $\varphi:\mathfrak{sl}_2\to S$ is a bijective Lie algebra homomorphism onto a subalgebra $S\subseteq\mathfrak{gl}_n$ (bracket $XY-YX$), put $V_i=\varphi(v_i)$, and let $\lambda_3$ and $\lambda_3'$ be the greatest and least eigenvalue of $V_3$ (eigenvalues ordered by real part). Let $v,v'\in\mathbb C^n$ satisfy $V_3v=\lambda_3v$ and $V_3v'=\lambda_3'v'$. Find, with proof, $V_1v$ and $V_2v'$.

pumac-2017-power-20b.prompt: **Problem 3.1.5(ii).** Let $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ have basis $v_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ with bracket $[A,B]=AB-BA$, so $[v_3,v_1]=2v_1$, $[v_3,v_2]=-2v_2$, $[v_1,v_2]=v_3$. Suppose $\varphi:\mathfrak{sl}_2\to S$ is a bijective Lie algebra homomorphism onto a subalgebra $S\subseteq\mathfrak{gl}_n$ (bracket $XY-YX$), put $V_i=\varphi(v_i)$, and let $\lambda_3$ and $\lambda_3'$ be the greatest and least eigenvalue of $V_3$ (eigenvalues ordered by real part). Let $v,v'\in\mathbb C^n$ satisfy $V_3v=\lambda_3v$ and $V_3v'=\lambda_3'v'$. Find, with proof, $\lambda_3$ and $\lambda_3'$. (You may use that $V_1v=0$ and $V_2v'=0$.)

pumac-2017-power-21.prompt: **Problem 3.1.6.** A *Lie algebra* is a complex vector space $L$ with a bilinear bracket $[\cdot,\cdot]:L\times L\to L$ such that $[x,x]=0$ and the Jacobi identity $[x,[y,z]]+[y,[z,x]]+[z,[x,y]]=0$ holds. Up to isomorphism, how many Lie algebras have dimension $1$? dimension $2$? List them all.
pumac-2017-power-21.answer: Dimension 1: one (abelian). Dimension 2: two, the abelian one and the one with basis $x,y$ and $[x,y]=x$.

pumac-2017-power-22a.prompt: **Problem 3.2.1(i).** A *subalgebra* $S$ of a Lie algebra $L$ is a subspace with $[x,y]\in S$ for $x,y\in S$; an *ideal* $I$ is a subalgebra with $[x,y]\in I$ for $x\in I$, $y\in L$. If $L$ is an abelian Lie algebra, show that any subspace of $L$ is a subalgebra and an ideal.
pumac-2017-power-22a.answer: All brackets are $0$, which lies in every subspace.

pumac-2017-power-22b.prompt: **Problem 3.2.1(ii).** A *subalgebra* of a Lie algebra $L$ is a subspace $S$ with $[x,y]\in S$ for all $x,y\in S$; an *ideal* $I$ is a subalgebra with $[x,y]\in I$ for $x\in I$, $y\in L$. Find a nonabelian Lie algebra of $n\times n$ matrices for some $n>2$ (bracket $XY-YX$) that has a subalgebra that is not an ideal. Specify the subalgebra and briefly justify why it is not an ideal.
pumac-2017-power-22b.answer: $L=\mathfrak{gl}_3$ with the diagonal matrices as subalgebra.

pumac-2017-power-23.prompt: **Problem 3.2.2.** Let $L$ be a subspace of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ and $I=\{x\in L: x\text{ nilpotent}\}$. Is $I$ a subalgebra? an ideal? Fully justify your responses.
pumac-2017-power-23.answer: In general neither: e.g. for $L=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ the nilpotent matrices $e_{12},e_{21}$ have bracket $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, which is not nilpotent.

pumac-2017-power-24.prompt: **Problem 3.2.3.** For subspaces $L_1,L_2$ of a Lie algebra $L$ let $[L_1,L_2]$ denote the span of all brackets $[v_1,v_2]$, $v_i\in L_i$. Is $[I,J]$ an ideal of $L$ for ideals $I,J$ of $L$?
pumac-2017-power-24.answer: Yes (with $[I,J]$ the span of the brackets).
pumac-2017-power-24.reviewNote: Taken literally, the printed set {[v1,v2]} of single brackets need not be closed under addition (for a free 2-step nilpotent Lie algebra on 4 generators, x1x2+x3x4 is not a single commutator); the answer uses the span, as in the official solution.

pumac-2017-power-25.prompt: **Problem 3.2.4.** Let $\varphi:L_1\to L_2$ be a Lie algebra homomorphism. Show that $\ker\varphi$ is an ideal of $L_1$ and $\operatorname{im}\varphi$ is a subalgebra of $L_2$.

pumac-2017-power-26a.prompt: **Problem 3.3.1(i).** Let $V_d$ be the real vector space of polynomials of degree at most $d$ (with real coefficients). Find $\dim V_3$ and a basis.

pumac-2017-power-26b.prompt: **Problem 3.3.1(ii).** On the space $V_2$ of real polynomials $p=\alpha_0+\alpha_1x+\alpha_2x^2$ of degree at most $2$ define the bracket $[p,q]=(\alpha_1\beta_2-\alpha_2\beta_1)+(\alpha_2\beta_0-\alpha_0\beta_2)x+(\alpha_0\beta_1-\alpha_1\beta_0)x^2$ for $q=\beta_0+\beta_1x+\beta_2x^2$ (this is a Lie algebra). Find a subspace $S$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ for some $n$ and an explicit isomorphism $V_2\to S$ preserving the bracket (where $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ has bracket $XY-YX$).

pumac-2017-power-27.prompt: **Problem 3.3.2.** Let $\mathbb R^2$ be given the abelian Lie bracket $[x,y]=0$. Find a subspace $S$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ for some $n$ and an explicit isomorphism $\mathbb R^2\to S$ of Lie algebras (bracket $XY-YX$ on $\mathfrak{gl}_n$).

pumac-2017-power-28.prompt: **Problem 3.4.1.** For $x$ in a Lie algebra $L$, the adjoint map is $\operatorname{ad}x:L\to L$, $(\operatorname{ad}x)(y)=[x,y]$. Verify that $\operatorname{ad}x$ is a linear map.
pumac-2017-power-28.answer: $[x,\cdot]$ is linear by bilinearity of the bracket.

pumac-2017-power-29a.prompt: **Problem 3.4.2(i).** For $x$ in a Lie algebra $L$, the adjoint map is $\operatorname{ad}x:L\to L$, $(\operatorname{ad}x)(y)=[x,y]$. $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ has basis $v_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ with $[v_1,v_2]=v_3$, $[v_3,v_1]=2v_1$, $[v_3,v_2]=-2v_2$. Explain how $\operatorname{ad}x$ can be thought of as an element of $\mathfrak{gl}_3$ when $x\in\mathfrak{sl}_2$.
pumac-2017-power-29a.answer: $\operatorname{ad}x$ is a linear map of the 3-dimensional space $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ to itself, so after choosing a basis it is a $3\times3$ matrix.

pumac-2017-power-29b.prompt: **Problem 3.4.2(ii).** For $x$ in a Lie algebra $L$, the adjoint map is $\operatorname{ad}x:L\to L$, $(\operatorname{ad}x)(y)=[x,y]$. $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ has basis $v_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ with $[v_1,v_2]=v_3$, $[v_3,v_1]=2v_1$, $[v_3,v_2]=-2v_2$. Find an explicit, nontrivial isomorphism from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ to a subalgebra of $\mathfrak{gl}_3$.
pumac-2017-power-29b.answer: $x\mapsto$ the matrix of $\operatorname{ad}x$ in the basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$; e.g. $v_1\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}0&0&-2\\0&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_2\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&0&2\\-1&0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $v_3\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(2,-2,0)$.

pumac-2017-power-30.prompt: **Problem 3.4.3.** For $x$ in a Lie algebra $L$, the adjoint map is $\operatorname{ad}x:L\to L$, $(\operatorname{ad}x)(y)=[x,y]$. Show that the set $\mathfrak t_3$ of $3\times3$ complex upper-triangular matrices is a Lie algebra under $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. Find a basis $e_1,\dots,e_6$ and write $\operatorname{ad}e_i$ explicitly for each basis vector. Find the eigenvalues of each $\operatorname{ad}e_i$.
pumac-2017-power-30.answer: Basis $E_{11},E_{22},E_{33},E_{12},E_{13},E_{23}$, $\dim 6$. $\operatorname{ad}E_{ii}$ are diagonal with eigenvalues in $\{0,\pm1\}$; $\operatorname{ad}E_{ij}$ ($i<j$) are nilpotent, all eigenvalues $0$.

pumac-2017-power-31.prompt: **Problem 3.4.4.** For $x$ in a Lie algebra $L$, the adjoint map is $\operatorname{ad}x:L\to L$, $(\operatorname{ad}x)(y)=[x,y]$. Show that $[x,y]=0$ implies $(\operatorname{ad}x)\circ(\operatorname{ad}y)=(\operatorname{ad}y)\circ(\operatorname{ad}x)$.

pumac-2017-power-32.prompt: **Problem 3.4.5.** For $x$ in a Lie algebra $L$, the adjoint map is $\operatorname{ad}x:L\to L$, $(\operatorname{ad}x)(y)=[x,y]$. Let $L\subseteq\mathfrak{gl}_n$ be a matrix Lie algebra. If $x$ is nilpotent, is $\operatorname{ad}x$ nilpotent? If $\operatorname{ad}x$ is nilpotent, is $x$ nilpotent? Justify.

pumac-2017-power-33.prompt: **Problem 3.4.6.** For $x$ in a Lie algebra $L$, the adjoint map is $\operatorname{ad}x:L\to L$, $(\operatorname{ad}x)(y)=[x,y]$. Show that $\operatorname{ad}x$ is a derivation: $(\operatorname{ad}x)([y,z])=[(\operatorname{ad}x)(y),z]+[y,(\operatorname{ad}x)(z)]$ for all $y,z$.
pumac-2017-power-33.answer: This is the Jacobi identity rewritten.

pumac-2017-power-34.prompt: **Problem 4.1.1.** For a Lie algebra $L$ the *Killing form* is $\kappa(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x\circ\operatorname{ad}y)$. Verify that $\kappa$ is symmetric and bilinear.
pumac-2017-power-34.answer: Linearity of $\operatorname{ad}$ and of trace, and $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$.

pumac-2017-power-35.prompt: **Problem 4.1.2.** With the Killing form $\kappa(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x\circ\operatorname{ad}y)$, show that $\kappa([x,y],z)=\kappa(x,[y,z])$.

pumac-2017-power-36.prompt: **Problem 4.1.3.** Let $L\subseteq\mathfrak{gl}_n$ be a Lie algebra whose Killing form is non-degenerate (a semisimple Lie algebra: $\kappa(x,y)=0$ for all $y$ implies $x=0$). Recall that a matrix is semisimple if it is diagonalizable. Show that $x\in L$ is semisimple if and only if $\operatorname{ad}x$ is semisimple (as a linear map $L\to L$).
pumac-2017-power-36.answer: ($\Rightarrow$) $\operatorname{ad}x$ is diagonalizable on $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ and hence on the invariant subspace $L$. ($\Leftarrow$) Jordan decomposition $x=s+n$: $\operatorname{ad}n$ is nilpotent and semisimple, hence $0$, so $n$ is central, hence $0$ by non-degeneracy.
pumac-2017-power-36.reviewNote: The converse direction uses the standard (unproved here) fact that the semisimple and nilpotent Jordan parts of an element of a semisimple matrix Lie algebra lie in that algebra; the official solution is also only a sketch.

pumac-2017-power-37a.prompt: **Problem 4.1.4(i).** Let $L$ be a Lie algebra with Killing form $\kappa$ and $I\subseteq L$ an ideal. Let $I'=\{x\in L:\kappa(x,y)=0\ \forall y\in I\}$. Show that $I'$ is also an ideal.
pumac-2017-power-37a.answer: Use $\kappa([x,z],y)=\kappa(x,[z,y])$ and that $I$ is an ideal.

pumac-2017-power-37b.prompt: **Problem 4.1.4(ii).** Let $L$ be a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form $\kappa$ (semisimple). A Lie algebra is *simple* if its only ideals are $\{0\}$ and itself. Show that $L=L_1\oplus\dots\oplus L_k$ (as Lie algebras, with $[L_i,L_j]=0$ for $i\ne j$) where each $L_i$ is a simple ideal of $L$.
pumac-2017-power-37b.answer: Split off a minimal ideal $I$ via $L=I\oplus I^\perp$ and induct on the dimension.
pumac-2017-power-37b.reviewNote: The proof cites Cartan's criterion (a Lie algebra with identically zero Killing form is solvable), which the paper does not prove; the official solution only sketches it.

pumac-2017-power-38.prompt: **Problem 4.2.1.** Let $L$ be a Lie algebra with a maximal toral subalgebra $H$ (an abelian subalgebra of semisimple elements) such that $L$ has a basis of simultaneous eigenvectors of $\operatorname{ad}h$, $h\in H$: $[h,v_i]=\lambda_i(h)v_i$. Show that each $\lambda_i:H\to\mathbb C$ is linear.

pumac-2017-power-39.prompt: **Problem 4.2.2.** In the setting of a Lie algebra $L$ with maximal toral subalgebra $H$ and a basis of simultaneous eigenvectors of $\operatorname{ad}H$, let $L_\lambda=\{v\in L:[h,v]=\lambda(h)v\ \forall h\in H\}$ for $\lambda\in H^*$. Show that $L$ is isomorphic as a vector space to $\bigoplus_{\lambda}L_\lambda$ (the sum over those $\lambda$ with $L_\lambda\neq0$).
pumac-2017-power-39.answer: $L=\sum L_\lambda$ because of the eigenbasis, and the sum is direct because eigenvectors for distinct functionals are independent.

pumac-2017-power-40.prompt: **Problem 4.2.3.** Let $L$ be a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form $\kappa$, a maximal toral subalgebra $H$ and root space decomposition $L=\bigoplus_\lambda L_\lambda$ (with $L_0=H$). For roots $\alpha,\beta$, determine the condition on $\alpha$ and $\beta$ under which $\kappa(v_1,v_2)\neq0$ for some $v_1\in L_\alpha$, $v_2\in L_\beta$.

pumac-2017-power-41.prompt: **Problem 4.2.4.** Let $L$ be a semisimple Lie algebra with maximal toral subalgebra $H$ and root space decomposition $L=H\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}L_\alpha$ ($L_0=H$, $\Phi$ the nonzero roots, $m_\alpha=\dim L_\alpha$). For $\lambda\in H^*$ let $t_\lambda\in H$ be the element with $\kappa(t_\lambda,h)=\lambda(h)$ for all $h\in H$, and $\langle\lambda,\mu\rangle=\kappa(t_\lambda,t_\mu)$. Assume the facts from the text that $\kappa|_H$ is non-degenerate, and that for each root $\alpha$ there is $h_\alpha\in H$ spanning, with elements of $L_{\pm\alpha}$, a copy of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with $\alpha(h_\alpha)=2$ (so the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{ad}h_\alpha$ are integers, by Problem 3.1.5). Show that $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is a symmetric bilinear form on $H^*$ that is positive definite on the real span $E$ of the roots.
pumac-2017-power-41.answer: Symmetric bilinear from $\kappa$; positivity from $\langle\lambda,\lambda\rangle=\sum_\alpha m_\alpha\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle^2$ with all $\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle$ rational.
pumac-2017-power-41.reviewNote: As printed the claim is that the form is an inner product on the complex space H*; a positive-definite statement only makes sense over the real span of the roots, which is what the proof shows (the official solution is a sketch).

pumac-2017-power-42.prompt: **Problem 4.2.5.** In the setting of a semisimple Lie algebra $L$ with maximal toral subalgebra $H=L_0$ and root spaces $L_\lambda$, let $t_\lambda\in H$ be defined by $\kappa(t_\lambda,h)=\lambda(h)$ for $h\in H$. Show that $[x,y]=\kappa(x,y)\,t_\lambda$ for $x\in L_\lambda$, $y\in L_{-\lambda}$.
pumac-2017-power-42.answer: $[x,y]\in H$ and pairing both sides against $h\in H$ gives equal values.

pumac-2017-power-43.prompt: **Problem 4.2.6.** For a root $\lambda$ let $e_\lambda\in L_\lambda$, $f_\lambda\in L_{-\lambda}$, $h_\lambda\in H$ span a copy of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ (with $h_\lambda=[e_\lambda,f_\lambda]$ and $\lambda(h_\lambda)=2$), and $t_\lambda\in H$ satisfies $\kappa(t_\lambda,h)=\lambda(h)$. Show that $h_\lambda=\dfrac{2t_\lambda}{\kappa(t_\lambda,t_\lambda)}$ and $\kappa(t_\lambda,t_\lambda)\kappa(h_\lambda,h_\lambda)=4$.

pumac-2017-power-44.prompt: **Problem 5.1.1.** Let $V$ be a real vector space with an inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. A subset $R\subset V$ (not a subspace) is a *root system* of $V$ if $\operatorname{span}R=V$ and for all $v,w\in R$: (1) the only scalar multiples of $v$ in $R$ are $\pm v$; (2) $w-\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}v\in R$; (3) $\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}\in\mathbb Z$. A root system is *reducible* if $R=R_1\cup R_2$ with nonempty $R_1,R_2$, $\langle v_1,v_2\rangle=0$ for $v_i\in R_i$, and each $R_i$ a root system (of its span); otherwise irreducible. A *base* $B\subset R$ is a basis of $V$ such that every $w\in R$ is $\pm\sum_{v\in B}c(v)v$ with integers $c(v)\ge0$. Find all root systems in $\mathbb R$.

pumac-2017-power-45.prompt: **Problem 5.1.2.** Let $V$ be a real vector space with an inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. A subset $R\subset V$ (not a subspace) is a *root system* of $V$ if $\operatorname{span}R=V$ and for all $v,w\in R$: (1) the only scalar multiples of $v$ in $R$ are $\pm v$; (2) $w-\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}v\in R$; (3) $\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}\in\mathbb Z$. A root system is *reducible* if $R=R_1\cup R_2$ with nonempty $R_1,R_2$, $\langle v_1,v_2\rangle=0$ for $v_i\in R_i$, and each $R_i$ a root system (of its span); otherwise irreducible. A *base* $B\subset R$ is a basis of $V$ such that every $w\in R$ is $\pm\sum_{v\in B}c(v)v$ with integers $c(v)\ge0$. For $v\neq\pm w$ in a root system, let $\varphi$ be the angle between them ($\langle v,w\rangle=\|v\|\|w\|\cos\varphi$). Using that $v,w$ may be interchanged in condition (3), show that $4\cos^2\varphi\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.
pumac-2017-power-45.answer: $4\cos^2\varphi$ is a product of two integers, nonnegative, and $<4$.

A subset $R\subset V$ (not a subspace) is a *root system* of $V$ if $\operatorname{span}R=V$ and for all $v,w\in R$: (1) the only scalar multiples of $v$ in $R$ are $\pm v$; (2) $w-\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}v\in R$; (3) $\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}\in\mathbb Z$. A *base* $B\subset R$ is a basis of $V$ such that every $w\in R$ is $\pm\sum_{v\in B}c(v)v$ with integers $c(v)\ge0$. Using the standard dot product, find all root systems of $\mathbb R^2$ up to rotation, dilation and (independent) rescaling of orthogonal components.
pumac-2017-power-46.answer: Four: $A_1\times A_1$ (e.g. $\pm(2,0),\pm(0,1)$), $A_2$ (6 roots, equal length, $60^\circ$ apart), $B_2$ (8 roots, lengths $1,\sqrt2$, $45^\circ$ apart), $G_2$ (12 roots, lengths $1,\sqrt3$, $30^\circ$ apart).
pumac-2017-power-46.reviewNote: The paper's ''up to rotation and dilation'' equivalence is ambiguous for A1xA1 (arbitrary relative lengths); I count it as one system, giving the same four systems as the official solution.

pumac-2017-power-49.prompt: **Problem 5.2.1.** Let $V$ be a real vector space with an inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. A subset $R\subset V$ (not a subspace) is a *root system* of $V$ if $\operatorname{span}R=V$ and for all $v,w\in R$: (1) the only scalar multiples of $v$ in $R$ are $\pm v$; (2) $w-\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}v\in R$; (3) $\dfrac{2\langle v,w\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}\in\mathbb Z$. A root system is *reducible* if $R=R_1\cup R_2$ with nonempty $R_1,R_2$, $\langle v_1,v_2\rangle=0$ for $v_i\in R_i$, and each $R_i$ a root system (of its span); otherwise irreducible. A *base* $B\subset R$ is a basis of $V$ such that every $w\in R$ is $\pm\sum_{v\in B}c(v)v$ with integers $c(v)\ge0$. Let $B$ be a base of a root system and normalize it to unit vectors $B'$; then $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\le0$ for $i\ne j$ and $4\langle v_i,v_j\rangle^2\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. The *Dynkin diagram* has a node for each element of $B'$ and $e(v,w)=4\langle v,w\rangle^2$ edges between $v$ and $w$ (an arrow pointing to the shorter root of the original base when $e\ge2$). Show that a root system is irreducible if and only if its Dynkin diagram is connected.
pumac-2017-power-49.answer: A partition of the base into orthogonal parts splits every root into one part, and conversely.

pumac-2017-power-50.prompt: **Problem 5.2.2.** Let $B$ be a base of a root system and normalize it to unit vectors $B'$; then $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\le0$ for $i\ne j$ and $4\langle v_i,v_j\rangle^2\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. The *Dynkin diagram* has a node for each element of $B'$ and $e(v,w)=4\langle v,w\rangle^2$ edges between $v$ and $w$ (an arrow pointing to the shorter root of the original base when $e\ge2$). Show that no Dynkin diagram may have a cycle.
pumac-2017-power-50.answer: For unit vectors $v_1,\dots,v_n$ with $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\le0$ and $2|\langle v_i,v_j\rangle|\ge1$ on edges, $\|\sum v_i\|^2>0$ forces fewer edges than vertices.

pumac-2017-power-51.prompt: **Problem 5.2.3.** Let $B$ be a base of a root system and normalize it to unit vectors $B'$; then $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\le0$ for $i\ne j$ and $4\langle v_i,v_j\rangle^2\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. The *Dynkin diagram* has a node for each element of $B'$ and $e(v,w)=4\langle v,w\rangle^2$ edges between $v$ and $w$ (an arrow pointing to the shorter root of the original base when $e\ge2$). Show that no node in a Dynkin diagram has more than three total edges attached to it (counting a double edge as $2$, a triple edge as $3$).
pumac-2017-power-51.answer: Project the unit vector $v$ onto the span of its (mutually orthogonal) neighbours: $\sum\langle v,v_i\rangle^2<1$.

pumac-2017-power-52.prompt: **Problem 5.2.4.** Let $B$ be a base of a root system and normalize it to unit vectors $B'$; then $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\le0$ for $i\ne j$ and $4\langle v_i,v_j\rangle^2\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. The *Dynkin diagram* has a node for each element of $B'$ and $e(v,w)=4\langle v,w\rangle^2$ edges between $v$ and $w$ (an arrow pointing to the shorter root of the original base when $e\ge2$). Assume the **Shrinking Lemma**: if a Dynkin diagram has nodes $v_1,\dots,v_n$ forming a line of single edges, then replacing them by the single node $v=\sum v_i$ (attached to whatever the ends were attached to) gives the Dynkin diagram of a base of a root system. Use it, together with Problems 5.2.2 and 5.2.3, to show that a connected Dynkin diagram cannot have more than one branch node (node with three neighbours), more than one double edge, or both a branch node and a double edge.
pumac-2017-power-52.answer: Shrink the single-edge path between two such features into one node, which would then have $4$ edges.

pumac-2017-power-53.prompt: **Problem 5.2.5.** Let $B$ be a base of a root system and normalize it to unit vectors $B'$; then $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\le0$ for $i\ne j$ and $4\langle v_i,v_j\rangle^2\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. The *Dynkin diagram* has a node for each element of $B'$ and $e(v,w)=4\langle v,w\rangle^2$ edges between $v$ and $w$ (an arrow pointing to the shorter root of the original base when $e\ge2$). Prove that if a connected Dynkin diagram has a double edge whose two ends are both attached to further nodes, then the diagram is $F_4$ (four nodes in a line with a double edge in the middle).
pumac-2017-power-53.answer: By 5.2.4 the diagram is a path $v_1\cdots v_m=w_n\cdots w_1$; Cauchy-Schwarz on the combined vectors gives $(m-1)(n-1)<2$.

pumac-2017-power-54.prompt: **Problem 5.2.6.** Let $B$ be a base of a root system and normalize it to unit vectors $B'$; then $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\le0$ for $i\ne j$ and $4\langle v_i,v_j\rangle^2\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. The *Dynkin diagram* has a node for each element of $B'$ and $e(v,w)=4\langle v,w\rangle^2$ edges between $v$ and $w$ (an arrow pointing to the shorter root of the original base when $e\ge2$). Consider a connected Dynkin diagram with a branch node $z$ (three neighbours). Show that one of the three arms from $z$ has length $1$ (a single node), and that for the other two arms: if one has length $1$ the third may have any length; if one has length $2$, the third has length at most $4$. (Arm lengths count nodes, not including $z$; all edges are single by Problem 5.2.4.)
pumac-2017-power-54.answer: With arm lengths $n\ge m\ge p$: $\frac1{n+1}+\frac1{m+1}+\frac1{p+1}>1$, giving $p=1$, and $m=1$ ($n$ arbitrary) or $m=2$, $n\le4$.

pumac-2017-power-55a.prompt: **Problem 5.3.1(i).** Let $E_{i,j}$ denote a matrix unit. Let $\mathfrak h$ be the diagonal matrices in the algebra, $\lambda_i$ the coordinate functionals $\lambda_i(\sum c_k(E_{k,k}-E_{k+n,k+n}))=c_i$ (and $\lambda_i(\operatorname{diag}(c))=c_i$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_n$). The Killing form restricted to $\mathfrak h$ is a positive multiple of $\sum c_ic_i'$ in each case below, so $\langle\lambda_i,\lambda_j\rangle\propto\delta_{ij}$ (direct computation of $\kappa(h,h')=\sum_{\text{roots}}\alpha(h)\alpha(h')$ gives $(4n-2)\sum c_ic_i'$ for $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}$, $2n\sum c_ic_i'$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_n$, $(4n+4)\sum c_ic_i'$ for $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}$). The Dynkin diagram is built from a base of the root system of $\mathfrak h^*$, as for $\mathfrak{so}_{2n}$ in the text (where $\{\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}\}\cup\{\lambda_{n-1}+\lambda_n\}$ is a base and the diagram is $D_n$).
